Save a setup as one JSON file

Source: R/setup.R
write_setup.Rd

Writes a setup to one JSON file that R code, a Shiny app and an agent can share. The file holds no key. An agent can edit the descriptions as text, and git shows the changes.

Usage

write_setup(setup, path)

Arguments

setup

A setup from decision_setup() or read_setup().

path

The path of the JSON file, in a folder that exists. An existing file is replaced.

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

The file holds one JSON object, indented with two spaces:

  • version: 1, the version of the layout.

  • decider: provider, base_url, model, format, image_format (null for OpenAI and OpenRouter) and input (null when the input type is not checked). It holds no key and no credentials function: read_setup() gives the decider its credentials.

  • questions: an object keyed by question name, in order. Each question has type ("noul", "choice" or "score"), instructions and answers: an object keyed by answer, in order, whose values are the descriptions (null for none).

  • references: null, or an object keyed by answer whose values are arrays of the prepared JPEG images, each in base64 on one line.

  • image_settings: max_size (null to keep the size), upscale and crop ("none", "center" or a box [x, y, width, height]).

  • calibrator: null, or the calibrator as base64 of serialize().

  • calibrator_hash: null, or the hash of all that changes the answers of the model when the calibrator was stored: the decider (provider, server URL, model, request format and image format), the questions, the references and the image settings. It is the hash of a path file of decide() (see read_setup()).

A crop function cannot be saved: give crop as "none", "center" or a box.

The file goes to a temporary file in the same folder first, which then replaces path, so a crash during the write leaves the previous file whole.

See also

Other setups: decision_setup(), read_setup()

Examples

refund <- question_noul("Does the message ask for a refund?")
setup <- decision_setup(decider_typesafe("jev-1.13.0"), list(refund = refund))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
write_setup(setup, path)
read_setup(path)
#> <decisions::decision_setup>
#> * Model: jev-1.13.0
#> * URL: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone
#> * Questions: refund (2 answers)
#> * Reference images: 0
#> * Image settings: max_size = 768, upscale = FALSE, crop = "none"
#> * Calibrated: no
